name: Ray Dobbins
equipment: Heavy canvas work jacket (counts as a leather jacket)
Tool bag (socket set, multimeter, wire strippers, electrical tape, zip ties, bolt cutters, hacksaw)
Mary Delaine crew ID and engine-room keys

weapons.name: Flare pistol (30/90, 1 shot, loud and bright)

features: Human Versatility (Human: +1 to all ability scores)
Jury-Rig (10 minutes + a Mechanics check to build, repair or bypass a device; DC by complexity)

Gadgets (2 uses per long rest: Spoof — disable a camera, lock or drone for 1 minute; Overclock — an ally's weapon or device gets +1d4 on its next roll; Patch — restore 1d8 + 3 to a vehicle or machine)
Trade Union (Blue-Collar Worker feature: tradespeople, truckers and rivermen treat him as one of their own, and he can always find out who has the tool, the part or the fuel)

personality.traits: I fix things when I am nervous, and I am nervous a lot. I explain how everything works whether or not anyone asked. I hum Merle Haggard under my breath.
personality.ideals: Anything that's broken can be fixed, or used for parts. That goes for people too, mostly.
personality.bonds: The Mary Delaine. I have kept her engines running for six years and she is tied up two miles downriver with nobody aboard. I am not leaving her to rust.
personality.flaws: I freeze when people shout at me, and I hate making decisions that are not about machinery. I will hide in an engine room for as long as anyone lets me.

appearance: Twenty-seven, medium height, stocky, sandy hair under a grease-stained John Deere cap, a sunburnt neck and forearms covered in small burn scars. Wears coveralls tied at the waist over a T-shirt, a canvas jacket, and steel-toe boots, and always has a tool in one hand.
backstory: Ray Dobbins dropped out of the community college diesel programme because he was already better than the instructors, and has worked on towboats on the Tamarack and the Mississippi since he was twenty. He is the deck engineer of the Mary Delaine, a 3,200-horsepower towboat that tied up below Lock and Dam No. 14 on Friday to wait for a lock slot. The captain gave the crew Saturday off for Ferry Days. Ray was eating a corn dog by the stage when the Ruth Ellen — a boat he knew, crewed by men he drank with — came up the ramp with nobody at the wheel. He went aboard with Denny Rourke. Denny came back bitten. Ray came back with Denny's blood on his jacket and a logbook in his hand.
